source.publication: US Executive Order (Section 301, Trade Act 1974) / NPR / Yahoo Finance

description: The US administration brought into force a new phase of global tariffs replacing the expiring 2026 global tariff regime: 10%-12.5% duties on 60 of the top US trading partners covering ~99.4% of US imports, imposed under Section 301 (forced-labor investigation). Imports of most EU products face a 15% rate. The administration additionally threatened a 50% tariff on a range of Canadian goods, 100% tariffs on generic drugs from 2028, and a 100% tariff on goods from any country levying a digital-services tax on US companies, and announced USMCA will NOT be renewed in its current form. This is a broad, dated trade HEADWIND to global goods trade — a margin/pricing drag on EU exporters, autos, industrials and import-dependent supply chains, and a partial tailwind to reshoring themes (BIOSECURE biomanufacturing, domestic industrials). Registered as a macro-backdrop trade event so the risk is documented and dated; the net per-sector call is Claude's.
